travel_articles.body:
Research checked 13 November 2026. Visa rules, health screening, ferry schedules and seasonal conditions change — confirm each with official sources shortly before you commit.

Sierra Leone is published on this guide as a connected cluster — the Sierra Leone country guide, the Tokeh and River Number Two destination, the Tokeh and River No.2 attraction, and two stay guides — The Place Resort, Tokeh and Hotel Barmoi, Freetown — while the travel-insights shelf had zero Sierra Leone stories. The country guide is explicit: "Sierra Leone's Freetown Peninsula coast is a strong starting point for a stay that values scenery, local hospitality and a slower pace. Tokeh and River Number Two provide different settings for accommodation and day visits, and their proximity should not obscure practical differences in access, services and community arrangements." That decision — which base, what to pace, how to transfer — is what this story answers.

The entry paperwork: visa, yellow fever, health declaration, Ebola screening

Three documents belong on the same checklist before you book a flight. First, a visa is required for most visitors. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) entry guidance states: $80 USD cash on arrival for most passport holders; $25 for African Union nationals; or apply online via the Sierra Leone eVisa portal with credit or debit card (each traveler needs a separate visa, including infants and children). Single-entry visas are valid for 90 days from issue for stays up to 30 days; multiple-entry visas are valid for 365 days with a maximum of 30 days per visit (FCDO, updated 19 June 2026, current 13 November 2026). The official tourism site's FAQs confirm the same on-arrival and e-visa options and note the reciprocal fee-waiver list for AU partner countries (checked 13 November 2026).

Second, a yellow fever vaccination certificate is mandatory for entry — you may be asked to show proof on arrival (official tourism FAQs, Health & Safety section; FCDO). Third, a health travel declaration must be completed online within 72 hours before travel via the Sierra Leone Health Travel Portal; keep the confirmation QR code or reference number and present it if requested (FCDO). Ebola screening measures are in place on arrival as a public health response to the WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern declaration; expect enhanced health screening and comply to avoid delays or refusal of entry/departure (FCDO).

Passport validity: your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date of your visa application (FCDO).

Arrival and the transfer reality: Lungi to the peninsula

Most first visits land at Lungi International Airport (FNA) on the north side of the Sierra Leone River. The official tourism site describes a ferry crossing (30–40 minutes, weather and traffic dependent) or a helicopter transfer (10 minutes) to reach Freetown on the south bank. The ferry is the standard route; the helicopter is a faster, premium option. Airport security fees of $25 for arriving and $25 for departing passengers are mandatory (official tourism site).

From Freetown, your base choice determines the onward transfer:

  • Freetown city (Lumley Beach, Aberdeen): Hotel Barmoi sits on Cape Road, Aberdeen, about 400 m from Lumley Beach and ~35 km from Lungi airport via the ferry + road combination.
  • Tokeh Beach: approximately 20 miles from Freetown near York, fishing and tourism economy, home to The Place Resort ("one of the largest and most attractive beaches in West Africa" per the Ministry of Tourism).
  • River Number Two: 15 km from Freetown, "where the emerald waters of a river meet the turquoise Atlantic Ocean" per the Ministry of Tourism, described as "one of Sierra Leone's most alluring and celebrated attractions."

The country guide's standing caution applies: "A road transfer should be planned with current advice. Airport connections require their own detailed plan and should not be treated as a short extension of a beach day. Confirm departure times, meeting points and responsibility for any separate transfer legs." Do not stack a peninsula arrival and a long excursion on the same day as an international flight.

The base choice: city, Tokeh, or River Number Two

The country guide frames the peninsula as a "strong starting point for a stay that values scenery, local hospitality and a slower pace" but warns that "Tokeh and River Number Two provide different settings for accommodation and day visits, and their proximity should not obscure practical differences in access, services and community arrangements."

  • Freetown city base (Hotel Barmoi, Lumley Beach/ Aberdeen) — urban energy, market access, airport-proximate on the south bank, evening dining variety, day-trip launch point for Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary (40 min drive, Western Area Forest Reserve) and Bunce Island (slavery-history ruins). Best if you want an arrival-night buffer and city amenities before committing to the coast.
  • Tokeh Beach base (The Place Resort) — resort-scale beach, self-contained villas, beachside dining, Western Area peninsula setting. The Ministry of Tourism describes Tokeh as "sparkling white sand, palms in the background and shining turquoise waters." Best for travelers who want a full beach resort experience and are comfortable with the ~20-mile road transfer from Freetown.
  • River Number Two base — intimate river-meets-ocean setting, 15 km from Freetown, Ministry of Tourism calls it "one of Sierra Leone's most alluring and celebrated attractions." Best for travelers who value the distinctive estuary landscape and a quieter coastal night.

Source: Sierra Leone Ministry of Tourism beach directory (tourism.gov.sl/beaches/, checked 12 November 2026); Sierra Leone Tourism official site beach listings (checked 13 November 2026); Trek Africa Guide country page framing (checked 13 November 2026).

Seasonality and the daily rhythm

The National Tourist Board's climate guidance (tourismsierraleone.com FAQs, checked 13 November 2026) sets the planning pattern:

  • Dry season: November–April — best for beach and coastal visits, lower rainfall, stable movement.
  • Wet season: May–October — torrential downpours, affects movement and coastal experience.
  • Harmattan: December–February — dry, dusty, temperatures up to 40°C.
  • Coastal temperatures: 23–30°C year-round.

The country guide adds: "Check weather and local coastal conditions for the actual dates. Rain can affect movement and the experience of the coast, while tides and currents need attention regardless of sunshine. Keep a flexible plan for an outing and ask the accommodation about recent conditions rather than relying on an old review." A beach photograph does not establish swimming conditions; tides and currents at River Number Two and Tokeh are dynamic and require local advice on the day.

Beyond the peninsula: what else the cluster connects to

The official tourism site lists top attractions that sit outside the peninsula day-trip radius but are reachable with a dedicated day or overnight:

  • Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary — 40 minutes from Freetown city centre, Western Area Forest Reserve.
  • Bunce Island — ruins reclaimed by vegetation, slavery history, boat access from Freetown.
  • Tiwai Island — pygmy hippos, 100+ bird species, primates, Gola rainforest edge.
  • Gola National Park — biodiversity hotspot, Liberia border, east of Kenema.
  • Bureh Beach — surfers' favourite, 4 km crescent, forest-backed, 1990s surf history.
  • York Beach — culture, history, wildlife combined with beach time, central peninsula.

EcoFest, birdwatching, hiking/trekking, surfing, and cultural experiences are the official activity categories (tourismsierraleone.com). Each requires a separate day and a confirmed guide; do not compress multiple attractions into one rushed outing.

Money, cards and daily practicalities

Currency is the Sierra Leonean Leone (SLL). The official tourism FAQs address accommodation and meal cost questions but publish no fixed figures — costs vary by property and season. The National Tourist Board advises: hire a driver, avoid night travel, use cash/ATM with caution (tourismsierraleone.com FAQs, Travelling Around Sierra Leone section). FCDO guidance on Sierra Leone is not detailed on card acceptance; treat a cash reserve in small USD denominations (for visa on arrival, tips, small purchases) plus a Visa/Mastercard for larger hotels as the working setup, and confirm card acceptance with your specific accommodation before travel.

Confirm before you book

  • Visa route and timeline before non-refundable commitments: $80 cash on arrival (exact USD notes) or e-visa at evisa.sl (credit/debit card); single-entry 90-day validity, max 30 days stay; confirm your nationality's fee and process with the Sierra Leone High Commission or embassy.
  • Yellow fever certificate and health declaration at booking stage: both are entry requirements; the online health declaration is completed within 72 hours before travel; keep the QR code/reference.
  • Ebola screening compliance: expect enhanced screening on arrival; non-compliance can mean delays or refused entry/departure.
  • Lungi-to-peninsula transfer as a booked service: confirm ferry or helicopter timing, road transfer to your specific property, and who is responsible for each leg; do not assume taxis or hotel shuttles are always available at the ferry terminal.
  • Base choice matched to your pace: Freetown for arrival-night buffer and city access; Tokeh for resort beach scale; River Number Two for intimate estuary setting. The country guide warns proximity does not mean interchangeability.
  • Season against your dates: dry season (Nov–Apr) for beach reliability; wet season (May–Oct) and harmattan (Dec–Feb) require flexible coastal plans.
  • Swimming and boat activities by local advice only: agree equipment, guiding, lifejacket provision and return arrangements; respect community rules and photography expectations.
  • Export license for precious stones: if buying gems or minerals, verify the export license; "any deals that appear too good to be true probably are" (FCDO customs rules).

Packing from official recommendations

  • Yellow fever vaccination certificate (original, for entry).
  • Health travel declaration QR code/reference (printed or digital, for border).
  • Cash USD in small denominations ($1, $5, $10, $20) for visa on arrival, airport fees ($25 arriving + $25 departing), tips, and small purchases.
  • Anti-malarial medication (malaria concern in wet season; consult travel-health professional).
  • Rain protection (light waterproof jacket) — rain affects movement and coastal experience regardless of season.
  • Reef shoes or water sandals for river/estuary entries and rocky shores.
  • Sun protection: wide-brim hat, high-SPF sunscreen, lightweight long sleeves for boat excursions.
  • Medication documentation: prescriptions in original packaging with doctor's note for controlled substances.
  • Insect repellent (DEET or picaridin) for evenings and forest visits.

Three questions travelers actually ask

Can I do Freetown, Tokeh and River Number Two in one trip? Yes, but treat each as a separate base night, not a day-trip hop. The country guide is explicit: proximity should not obscure practical differences in access and services. A realistic shape is: night 1 Freetown (arrival buffer, Tacugama/Bunce Island), night 2–3 Tokeh or River Number Two (coastal pace), night 4 Freetown (pre-departure). Compressing the peninsula into day trips from Freetown loses the "slower pace" the country guide recommends.

Is the ferry reliable enough to build a plan around? The official tourism site gives a 30–40 minute ferry window, weather and traffic dependent. Build a buffer: do not schedule an international departure within 4 hours of your planned ferry arrival at Lungi. The helicopter option (10 minutes) is a premium hedge if your dates are tight and the service is operating — confirm directly with the operator.

Do I need a travel agent for a first Sierra Leone trip? Not mandatory, but the transfer complexity (ferry + road, timing buffers, base-specific logistics) and the health declaration/Ebola screening requirements make an agent a practical time-saver for first visits. The National Tourist Board's FAQ section on travelling around Sierra Leone recommends hiring a driver and avoiding night travel — an agent typically arranges this as a bundled service.

Continue planning

  • Tokeh and River No.2 attraction — the easy coast escape with striking beaches, tide and sea-state caution, community settings, transfer realism.
  • The Place Resort, Tokeh — self-contained villas, beachside dining, Agoda booking via Stay22.
  • Hotel Barmoi, Freetown — oceanfront rooms on Cape Road, Aberdeen, pool/gym/restaurant, exact Booking.com booking option via Stay22.
